1.1: *The Palaces of Rabbi Ishmael, which he saw when he ascended on High, and the Work of the Chariot*
1.2: Rabbi Ishmael said: What are these songs that he who seeks to gaze upon the vision of the Chariot says, so that he may ascend in peace and descend in peace? Greater than all of these is for him to be attended to, that they might usher him in and bring him into the chambers of the Palaces of Arabot of the firmament, and station him to the right of the Throne of Glory. At times he stands there until the proclamation of the Lord God of Israel, to see what they do before the Throne of Glory and to know what is destined to occur in the world. 2 Whom they humble and whom they exalt; whom they weaken and whom they strengthen; whom they impoverish and whom they enrich; whom they put to death and whom they bring to life; from whom they take away an inheritance and to whom they grant an inheritance; to whom they bequeath Torah and to whom they give wisdom. 3 Greater than all of these is that he beholds all the deeds of the sons of men which they perform even in the innermost chambers, whether they be fair deeds or corrupted deeds. If a man has stolen, he knows and recognizes it; if a man has committed adultery, he knows and recognizes it; if a man has murdered, he knows and recognizes it; if he is suspected regarding the menstruant, he knows and recognizes it; if he has spoken slander, he knows and recognizes it.
1.3: Greater than all of these is that he recognizes all those who know sorcery. 4 Greater than all of these is that all creatures shall be before him like silver before a refiner at the mouth of the furnace—which silver is pure and which silver is unfit. Even so shall he behold families like a man [beholds]: how many mamzerim are in the family, how many children of a menstruant are in the family, how many who are crushed of testicle or severed of member, how many sons of slaves, how many sons of profaned priests. 5 Greater than all of these is that he shall be set apart from all sons of men, and distinguished from all his peers, and honored above over those above and those below. Whoever harms the son of discernment, great and evil afflictions, sinful and harsh, fall upon him from heaven. Whoever stretches out a hand [against him], immediately the Court on High stretches out a hand against him. Greater than all of these: for anyone who lifts a hand against him and strikes him, they clothe him and cover him in leprosy, and they crown him with [the opposite of] glory. Greater than all of these: for anyone who speaks slander against him, they cast and throw upon him all manner of plagues, growths, and bruised wounds, from which moist boils flow.

2.1: Greater than all of these: for anyone who turns his face away from him [in rejection], they dim the light of the pupils of his eyes. Greater than all of these: for anyone who despises him, he shall have no remnant, nor survivor, nor heir. Greater than all of these: for anyone who speaks of his disgrace, they bring upon him destruction and a strict decree, and they show him no mercy. 2. Greater than all of these: as for those who kiss and smell and embrace and kiss, and afterward ostracize and mention [him for evil]—they are ostracized and excommunicated three times every day. The Glory on High says: From the day that permission was granted to the princes, to the worthy ones, to the clouds and the thick mists, and to the Cherubim and Seraphim, to descend and ascend in the Chariot—unto this day, by the Lord God of Israel, and by His Throne of Glory, and by the Crown of His head, by the Court on High and by the Glory on High, and by all the host of the heights and all His ministers: [cursed is] anyone who stands before him—he who gazes upon the Chariot—and then abandons him. 3. Rabbi Ishmael said: Thus they would teach concerning the vision of the Chariot: He who gazes upon the Chariot need only stand before three ranks: before a king, before a High Priest, and before the Sanhedrin. As for the Sanhedrin itself, it is obvious [he is] like a Prince; and if he is like a Prince, he shall not even stand before the Sanhedrin. And if he did stand, he forfeits his life—whoever he stood before—for he [thereby] diminishes his days and shortens his years. Rabbi Ishmael said: What is the nature of the songs that a man sings as he descends to the Chariot? He opens and says: The head of songs, the beginning of praise, and the start of song.
2.2: The beginning of rejoicing and the start of song do the ministering princes sing every day before Your decree, O Lord God of Israel, before His Throne of Glory. Behold, they lift an eye toward the Throne of Glory, high and exalted, the seat of the Most High. The precious vessel, through which wonder upon wonder was performed, sounded a great shout. May You surely gladden the King over You, as the joy of groom and bride in a house of joy; and let all the seed of Jacob exult when they come to take refuge under Your wings, like the joy of heart that rejoices thus; for your conversation is with the King’s conversation, and with your Creator you recount, as it is said: "Holy, Holy, Holy" is the Lord, with the praise and song of each and every day, with the rejoicing and song of every season, from the utterance that proceeds from the mouth of the Holy One, and from the melody that passes from the mouth of the ministers. Behold, fire, clouds, and flame pass away, are hidden, and are given every single day, as it is said: "Holy, Holy, Holy … "

3.1: Why are you terrified, O faithful servant of the King? Why are you trembling, O beloved minister? He said before Him: "If only, O Lord God of Israel! If I do not become terrified of fire, who is it that shall be terrified? If I do not tremble because of fire, who is it that shall tremble? For I am summoned to the Presence [Gevurah] six hours every day, and a thousand times they push me upon my knees until I reach Your Throne of Glory." And the Voice replied and said to him: "How many lips … let there be a voice from above the firmament, etc." Those who perform all these deeds for you—there is no shame upon their words, and there is none who contradicts their speech. The ministers of My splendor are called "the king of splendor"; He dwells in the chambers of the Palace of Silence, [amidst] awe, fear, holiness, and purity, as it is said: "Engraved" … The King of miracles, the King of mighty deeds, the King of wonders, the King of separateness.
3.2: Your Throne is a flying Throne; from the time He established the peg and the four fabrics in the wheel of the world, and all of it stands upon it for sixty thousand [years] and generations without end, and yet its feet have not been placed upon the ground of the Arabot firmament; rather, like a fluttering bird it stands at Your gate, the beauty of the exalted ones, the binders of crowns, and all the angels of the heads of the realms, the hosts are girded Bound and standing beneath Your Throne of Glory, and they were lifting them with the force of might and strength; yet even they did not set their feet upon the ground of the seven firmaments, but like a hovering bird they stand beneath it. Three times each and every day Your Throne of Glory would prostrate itself before You and say to You: "May it be Your will, O Lord God of Israel, that You be honored and sit upon me as a glorified King, for Your burden is beloved to me and is not heavy for me," as it is said: H[oly], H[oly], H[oly] is the Lord. A wondrous pride and an extraordinary dominion, a pride of exaltation and a dominion of majesty in which the Angel of the Presence conducts himself three times each and every day in the Heavenly Court before the Throne of Glory when he goes.
3.3: And the throne of the firmament which is upon the heads of the Cherubim, and upon the heads of the Ophanim, and upon the heads of the Holy Creatures—the Cherubim, the Ophanim, and the Holy Creatures are bound and standing beneath Your Throne of Glory. And when all those in the heights would see them as he goes—and the throne of the firmament that is upon the heads of the Cherubim, and upon the heads of the Ophanim, and upon the heads of the Holy Creatures—they tremble, are terrified, faint, and fall backward; for within one hundred and eighty-five thousand myriads of parasangs, no creature is able to touch that place because of the rivers of fires that gush // and go out from the mouths of the Cherubim, and from the mouths of the Ophanim, and from the mouths of the Holy Creatures, who open their mouths to say "Holy" at the hour when Israel says before Him "Holy," as it is said: H[oly], H[oly], H[oly] is the Lord of H[osts]. A measure of holiness, a measure of power, an awesome measure, a terrified measure, a measure of quaking, a measure of trembling, a measure of panic, a measure of shuddering, of the division of the splendors of YHWH God of Israel, Who is enthroned and sits well upon His Throne of Glory, which is engraved and entirely filled, from within and from without, [with the name] Lord, Lord. And the eye of no creature is able to gaze upon Him—neither the eyes of flesh and blood, nor the eyes of // His ministers.
3.4: And one who gazes at Him, or peeps, or sees them—shudders seize him for ever and ever and ever; his eyes discharge and emit [fluid]. before the fire, and they inflame him and they burn him; for the fire that goes out from the man who gazes inflames him and burns him. Why? Because of the likeness of the vision of the hollow of Hadarniel YHWH God of Israel, who governs and comes from His Throne of Glory. Pleasant and sweet is His mouth, like the appearance of the beauty of the radiance of the splendor of the eyes of the Holy Creatures, as it is said:

4.1: Who is like our King, according to all the prophets who lay hold of the kingdom? Who is like our Creator? Who is like YHWH, who was in the firmness of the knots of the crowns? For with six voices they sing before the Attribute of those who bear His Throne of Glory—the Cherubim, the Ophanim, and the Holy Creatures—with each voice being more sublime than its fellow and distinct from the one preceding it. The first voice: everyone who hears it is immediately afflicted and prostrates himself. The second voice: everyone who listens to it immediately goes astray and never returns. The third voice: everyone who hears it is seized by a convulsion and immediately dies. The fourth voice: everyone who listens to it, his skull and his stature are immediately broken, and most of the heads of his ribs are detached. The fifth voice: everyone who hears it is immediately poured out like a flagon, and his whole being turns to blood. The sixth voice: everyone who listens to it, a stabbing pain immediately seizes the heart, and his heart clamors and turns over the innards of his bowels, and the flow of his bile within him becomes like water, as it is said: H[oly], H[oly], H[oly]. Who is like our King? Who is like our Creator? Who is like YHWH our God? He emits and brings forth from the crown of His head the sun and the moon, the Pleiades and Orion, the stars and Venus, the constellations.
4.2: Stars and constellations emerge and go out from His division, where He governs and sits upon His Throne of Glory. And a great light was emitted from between His eyes—King of miracles, and mighty King, and King of wonders, and King of abstinence is He, as it is said: H[oly], H[oly], H[oly]. Rabbi Ishmael said: All these songs Rabbi Akiva heard when he descended to the Merkavah, and he seized and learned them from before the Throne of Glory who were entreating to appease him from his purpose. Rabbi Ishmael said: That day was the fifth day of the week when a harsh report came from Rome, from the great metropolis of Rome, saying: "Seize four men from the nobles of Israel: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, Rabbi Ishmael ben Elisha, Rabbi Eleazar ben Dama, and Rabbi Judah ben Bava." These were four of the nobles of Israel, and eight thousand disciples of the wise from Jerusalem were still theirs. When Rabbi Nehuniah ben ha-Kanah saw this decree, he arose and brought me down to the Chariot, and I requested an inquiry from Surya, the Prince of the Presence. He said to me: "Ten [names] were written upon the celestial linen and given to the wicked Samael, the prince of Rome, saying to you: 'And the striking of the nobles of Israel—at every favorable time it shall descend and [lay upon the] shoulder to fulfill the decree of "the abandonment of a man and his selling," etc.'"
4.3: But vengeance is stored up for Him to take revenge upon him, until the visitation of YHWH reaches the host of the height, etc., so that he and all the princes of the kingdoms shall be slaughtered and cast down like priests, like kids and lambs of the Day of Atonement.

5.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: All these conditions—yea, all these conditions—they stipulated and conditioned with the wicked Samael, and he said: "I have accepted them upon myself, that these ten mighty ones shall be destroyed." Rabbi Ishmael said: What did Hadariel YHWH God of Israel do at that hour? It was not enough for Him, and He said to the scribe: "Write decrees and great plagues—fierce and harsh, awesome and terrifying, heavy and diverse—upon wicked Rome," because of the wrath with which He was filled against Samael, who had accepted all these conditions upon himself. Rather, He immediately sent a messenger and wrote concerning it a day of vengeance that is destined and stored up for wicked Rome: "One cloud shall ascend and stand above Rome, and it shall bring down moist boils for six months upon man and upon beast, upon silver and upon gold, upon the fruits and upon every vessel." metals, and afterward another cloud shall ascend and push aside its companion and remain in its place for six other months and bring down a cloud of leprosy, and scab, and bright spot, and all kinds of plagues—all of them upon Rome—until a man shall say to his fellow: "Take for yourself wicked Rome and all that is in it for a single peruta," and he will say: "I have no need of it."

Rabbi Ishmael said: When I came and bore this testimony from before the Throne of Glory, all the fellows rejoiced, and they made that day before Rabbi Akiva ben Joseph a day of feasting and joy. Not only that, but the Prince said in joy: "Set before us all kinds of music and the drinking of wine, since the Holy One, blessed be He, the God of Israel, is destined to execute vengeance and wonders and the wonders of wonders upon her, upon wicked Rome." 5.3: 3. Rabbi Ishmael said: What did the celestial ones [clothed in] linen do at that hour? They commanded the angels of destruction, and they descended and executed upon him, upon Lupinus Caesar, a complete and decreed destruction, and there did not remain in all his palace a remnant or survivor. And the beautiful wife of Azariah, and all her ladies, and all his handmaidens, and all his concubines were cast down before him; and all his sons and all the members of his household and all the delights of his eye were mangled and cast down before him.
5.4: 4. What did they do to that wicked one? They took him and immersed him among his dead. Why? Because they were cast down before him, and whenever any person stretched out his hand to take one of the dead of Lupinus Caesar to place him upon the bier and take him out for burial, the abyss would swallow him; but as soon as he withdrew his hand from him, the abyss would vomit him up. And they were cast down before him, and furthermore, they rotted and stank before him before him . In his kingdom, he was ashamed before the princes of the kingdoms who were entering and departing before him.

6.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Surya, the Prince of the Presence, said to me: "Beloved, I shall tell you—all this shame, and all this disgrace, and all this humiliation for that wicked one, why [is it]? It is on account of Hananiah ben Teradion, whom they burned [with fire] all around him." upon him to kill him. They said to him: "My lord Caesar, relent concerning that sage, that he not be killed." He said: "Let him die, and all these members of his household, and even all Rome shall perish with him, and in this matter, I do not relent." 2. Rabbi Ishmael said: Suria, Prince of the Face, said to me: "My friend, I shall tell you why the power of that wicked one is so strong: because he is from the lineage of Esau the wicked; therefore, he is bold and strong, and his heart is hardened." 3. Rabbi Ishmael said: Suria, Prince of the Face, said to me: "Go, say to Rabbi Hananiah ben Teradion: Do not be grieved by this measure through which you depart to your eternal home, for already Hadriel, the Lord God of Israel, has filled His mouth with laughter and mocked that wicked one on your account." He said: "Hadar Niyon, awesome palace, Sha'at Tribu Saslusi Bo Sha'it, exalted is He who uprooted the uncircumcised, until He gives that wicked one a taste of the light of the fire from the rivers of the Cherubim, the Ophanim, and the Holy Creatures within Gehenna, for the sake of Rabbi Hananiah ben Teradion." 4.
6.2: Rabbi Ishmael said: Suria, Prince of the Face, said to me: "My friend, I shall tell you what the Pure Majesty, Radiance, Glory, Light, YHS, the Lord God of Israel, did: at that hour He cried out, and I descended and drove out and pushed Lupinus Caesar from his palace where he was sleeping on the ninth night, and I led them into the house of Linentinaris and T'fachim, and I brought in Rabbi Hananiah and led him into the palace of Lupinus Caesar. On the morrow, the executioners came who had taken Rabbi Hananiah, to speak wonders, and it was well; and he acted in the house of study, sitting and teaching the mighty ones of Israel. They lopped off his head—[for] Lupinus Caesar appeared to them in the likeness of Rabbi Hananiah ben Teradion—and they cut off his head, while Rabbi Hananiah ben Teradion was within his own house." 5. Rabbi Hananiah ben Teradion donned the royal crown and reigned over wicked Rome in the form of the face of Lupinus Caesar for six months. And he killed therein six thousand governors and a thousand thousand officials every single month. And they set up [the one] in the likeness of Rabbi Hananiah ben Teradion before the children of wicked Rome, and they were caught, and they cast him into the fire—and who was it that they cast into the fire? Lupinus Caesar.
6.3: For when they killed him, they returned and revived him by the glory of the dew from above. They seized him and cast him into the fire, and he was like a brand within the conflagration. All the , the Sages of Israel, yearned for him; for he would go forth from the Aravot firmament, proclaiming and saying the glory of the Above—namely, the thought which wicked Rome conceived against the princes of Israel to destroy them—Hadriel, the Lord God of Israel, concurred with it. Even the meditation of the heart that Rome meditates, it is to you as a response, as if you had [already] performed it.

7.1: Suria, the Prince of the Presence, my friend, the praise of the King and His throne, said to me: Therefore it is said, "Thy throne of glory upon a high cherub Hast Thou exalted, and the Ophanim of greatness bear it up." And creatures of frost, and creatures of vapor, and creatures of burning fire rule in majesty, and with [the names] YH and Sh-n and Shaddai they are borne. They were wrapped beneath Him like hinds under the plow, and there was a transformation upon their heads like the appearance of ice and prophecy, according to that which is said: "Holy, Holy, Holy," etc. 2. Be glorified, be exalted, be uplifted, O magnificent King who is upon a throne high and lifted up; awesome and terrifying art Thou, dwelling in the chambers of the palace of majesty. Thy servants and Thy throne are terrified and trembling; Aravot is Thy footstool. Every day with a voice of joy not awake with the roar of music and the multitude of song, as it is said: "Holy, Holy, Holy." 3. Awake, O strength, and from the movements of the Shekhinah, making the sound of resonance, wafting song and rebuke at the voice of the holy ones, at the voice of the servants, at the voice of the mighty ones, at the voice of the majestic ones, with a sweet palate and the pleasantness of the holy ones, Dweller in Ranzon. Rivers of flame bear up the circuit of the Throne of Glory.
7.2: This is the entire procedure, just as Rabbi Ishmael said: "What is the distinction of the song of the four crowned with beauty, who crown crowns from the roar of the Most High? Like a song of joy, exalt the Lord of flame! For in the Presence of the Face, the Presence of majesty, the splendor of splendors, you encamp; make your name wondrous. The soaring of our servant has separated you from the watch of the Chariot. He who mentions one Name: a soaring of blazing fire, flame surrounding, brilliance encompassing the rivers of radiance of the dwellings, as it is said: Holy, Holy, Holy, the Lord, my precious one, awesome in my generations."
7.3: Blessed of the Most High, exalted of the Most High; at times of glorious speech, pleasant and lovely at the time when they speak and proclaim before the Glorified King. Servants of awesome splendors; the King who sits in the palaces—the palace of silence, dread, awe, and holiness, as it is said: Holy, Holy, Holy.

8.1: Those who annul the decree, who revoke the oath, who remove wrath, who turn back jealousy, who mention love, who arrange songs before the majesty of the pride of the awesome palace. Why are you agitated and why do your hearts beat? Why are you joyful? Why do you appear pleasant [yet] terrified? They said: When a decree is issued from the laws, we stand in great terror; and when the radiances of the Shekhinah shine, we rejoice with great joy, as it is said: Holy, Holy, Holy (2).
8.2: At times pleasant, at times glorious, at times of beauty, at times of flame is the face of the Lord God of Israel, when He sits upon His throne of glory, and His exaltation is established in the seat of His majesty. His beauty is more lovely than the beauty of mighty deeds; His majesty is more excellent than the majesty of bridegrooms and brides in their bridal chamber. One who gazes upon Him—his eyes are immediately torn out, and at His beauty his frame is immediately poured out. And those who serve Him today do not and his eyes serve Him tomorrow, and those who serve Him tomorrow do not serve Him today, for their strength has weakened and their faces have blackened, and their heart has strayed and their eyes have become disordered after the majesty of the radiance of the beauty of their King, as it is said: Holy, Holy, Holy (3).
8.3: Beloved servants, handsome servants, hastening servants, swift servants—those stationed upon the stone of the throne of glory, and those who are served upon the wheels of the Merkavah. When the stone of the throne of glory turns upon them, the throne of the wheels of the Merkavah snatches them away. Those stationed to the right return and stand to the left, and those stationed to the left return and stand to the right; those stationed in front return and stand and stand behind behind; they return and stand in front. He who sees this one says, "This is he," and he who sees that one says, "This is he," because the features of his face of this one is like the countenance of that one. Happy is the King for whom this is His servant, and happy is their servant for whom this is their King. Happy is their King; the eye that glimpses and gazes upon this wondrous light—a wondrous and very, very strange sight—as it is said: Holy, Holy, Holy L. Rivers of joy, rivers of gladness, rivers of exultation, rivers of song, rivers of love, rivers of friendship pour forth and emerge from before the Throne of Glory, and they grow stronger and go through the gates of Arabot and the firmament from the sound of the sparkling of the wings of their Hayyot, from the sound of the beating of their Ofanim, from the sound of the singing of the cymbals of the Cherubim; it grows stronger and emerges with a great noise in holiness at the hour when Israel says "Holy" before Him, as it is said: Holy, Holy, Holy L.

9.1: Like the sound of the seas, like the noise of rivers, like the sound of Tarshish which the southern wind awakens in them , like the sound of the song of the Throne of Glory when it praises the King and sings to the Glorified King. A multitude of sounds and a great noise; many sounds were surrounding the Throne of Glory to help and strengthen it when it sings and praises the Mighty One of Israel, as it is said: Holy, Holy, Holy L. Blessed are you from the mouth of the Might of heaven and earth and those who descend to the Merkavah. If you would say and tell my children what I do during the Morning Prayer and Evening Prayer and during the Afternoon Prayer every single day and at every hour that Israel says "Holy" before Me: Teach them and say to them, "Lift your eyes to the firmament toward your house of prayer at the hour that you say 'Holy' before Me, for I have no pleasure in all My world that I created like that hour when your eyes are raised to My eyes and My eyes are raised to your eyes at the hour that you say 'Holy' before Me. For the voice that emerges from your mouth at that hour rises before Me like a pleasing aroma." And testify to them: what testimony do you see of Me? What I do to it—to the countenance of the face of Jacob their father, which is engraved for Me upon My Throne of Glory.
9.2: For at the hour when you say "Holy" before Me, I bow over it, and I fondle it, and I embrace it, and I kiss it. it and the beauty upon His dwelling three times, corresponding to the three times that you say "Holy" before Him, as it is said: Holy, Holy, Holy, three times. Who would not glorify the glorified King? Who would not praise the praised King? Who would not sanctify the Holy King? For every single day, many mighty deeds and wonders are renewed before Him, superior and distinct from one another. For from the breath of the eyelids of the Princes of Pel, His garments are dark, and there goes out from their mouths like eighty [myriads] … those [who name?] the Name, the Name that enters the ear and exits the mouth and is praised as above, King of kings, who has no equal, as it is said: Holy, Holy, Holy is the Lord. For in the place where they mention Him, He shines and gleams more than gold and silver, and pure chrysolite, diamond, sapphire, emerald, and carbuncle, and pure marble. For He is wondrous and exalted and swift and great, for in creating heaven and earth with it, all the orders of Creation were absorbed and restrained and rose and were sealed by it, as it is said: Holy, Holy, Holy.

10.1: Exalt yourselves, exalt yourselves, O masters of exaltation! Exalt yourselves, exalt yourselves, O masters of Gehenna; pass through, pass through, masters of Might; exalt yourselves, exalt yourselves, O masters of Pride. For to the King of the universe alone and to all His ministers belong exaltation, might, and pride and existence. For it is fitting for the minister of our God to be prideful and to rule; the Throne of His Glory is worthy of prevailing. For from the Throne of His Glory and above—Shema’as and Mahat thousand myriads of parasangs is His height and from the Throne of His Glory and below—Shema and Mahat thousand myriads of parasangs; His stature is one hundred and one thousand myriads of parasangs; His breadth—no eye has seen, O God, besides You; and the stature and breadth of His Name, blessed be His Name and His remembrance for ever and ever, Amen, and may it be so, and you shall say Amen, Hallelujah, we give thanks and from His right arm to His left arm is seventy-seven thousand myriads of parasangs in breadth. 2. For how many mighty deeds are the fringes of and the holiness of the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He, is like ten myriads of myriads, and His height the Throne of Glory of this mighty King—they carry and guard [it] day and night, evening, morning, and afternoon, in trembling, in haste, in dread, in quaking, in shaking, and in awe. And how much power is in the Throne of the minister of our God, that you sound for the remembrance of His Name in the height of the world, without limit and without number, with a voice of strength, as it is said: Holy, Holy, Holy. [3]. A decree of heaven is upon you, O descendents to the Merkavah, if you do not tell and say what you have heard.
10.2: And if you do not revere it, [given] that you have seen time after time exaltation and might, pride and majesty, which exalt themselves and uplift themselves, uplift themselves and elevate themselves, and take pride, becoming high and surging three times each and every day on high, and human beings do not know or recognize them.
10.3: The first section is finished; we shall begin The Middle Section

11.1: When the Angel of the Presence enters to extol and glorify before His Glory and to prepare a seat for the Mighty One of Jacob, he binds a body of sefisa crowns for the Ofanim of Splendor, for each and every one of them on its head; and a thousand thousand times he bows and falls and prostrates before each and every one of them. Six thousand crowns he binds for the Cherubim of Glory, for each and every one of them on its head, and six thousand times he bows and falls and prostrates before each and every one of them.
