11.2: And those angels who seek to sing a song before the Holy One, blessed be He, but they do not permit them until the time of the song of Israel arrives, as it is said: "When the morning stars sang together" (Job 38:7), and afterward, "and all the sons of God shouted for joy"—these are Israel. … the Lord God of Israel; His heart rejoices at the time of His children's prayer. And He threshes and finds for His beloved a Chariot. At the hour they stand before His Throne of Glory three times a day: When the dawn arrives, the King of Splendor sits and blesses the Living Creatures. To the Throne of the Living Creatures, He says to all the creatures, making them hear: "Living Creatures, Living Creatures who bear the Throne of My Glory with a whole heart and a willing soul—blessed be the hour in which I created you, exalted be the constellation in which I formed you, may the light of that day shine when you arose in thought upon My heart, for you are precious vessels that I prepared and fashioned. Silence for Me the voice of all the creatures I have created, and hear and harken to the voice of My children's prayer three times each and every day." When the afternoon prayer arrives, the King of Splendor sits and exalts the Living Creatures. Before a word can leave the mouth of the Holy Living Creatures, they emerge from beneath the Throne of Glory in full flight, their wings full of joy, their hands singing, and their feet dancing and laughing.
11.3: They surround their King, one to His right and one to His left, one before Him and one behind Him. They embrace and kiss Him and uncover their faces. They uncover [their faces] and the King of Glory covers His face, and the Arabot firmament is split like a sieve Like a little splendor and the radiance of the beauty of the form of the desire of the compassion of longings and the brilliance of the treasury of praise. The appearance of their faces is like the thing that was said: "Holy, Holy, Holy."
11.4: And those Living Creatures have six wings on their hands and feet, for each and every one of them, and with them they cover their faces and their feet so that they do not gaze upon the glory of the Shekhinah.

12.1: Annullers of the decree, witnesses of the oath, removers of wrath, averters of accusation, mentioners of love—the love of Abraham—before their King. When they see Him, that He is angry with His children, what do they do? They beat their wings and shake their loins and … upon their heads and fall upon their faces and say: "Release, release, Creator of the Beginning; forgive," said Jacob; "pardon, pardon, Holy One of Israel! For You are the Mightiest of kings (3 times). Awesome King, Terrifying King, Precious King, Honored King—why should You have enmity with the seed of Abraham? Why should You have jealousy with the seed of Isaac? Why should You have strife with the seed of Jacob? For how small are the heavens … "
12.2: At the time they say: "Release, release, Creator of the Beginning; forgive," said Jacob; "pardon, pardon, Holy One of Israel! For You are the Mightiest of kings (3 times). Awesome King, Terrifying King, Precious King, Honored King—why should You have enmity with the seed of Abraham? Why should You have jealousy with the seed of Isaac? Why should You have strife with the seed of Jacob? For how small are the heavens and the earth and all that is in them, and all their host, and all their multitude, and all their legions, and all their Seraphim, and all the Holy Living Creatures, and all the Ofanim of the Chariot, and all the wheels of the Chariot, and all the Hasmalim of the Chariot, and all the Throne of Glory, and all the holy palaces, and all the hidden stores of the heights, and all the treasuries of the firmament, and all the dwellings of heaven, and all the Zebulim of heaven, and all the Arabot of heaven, and all the heaven of heavens, and all the earth and all its depths, and all its seas, and all its rivers, and all its streams, and all its mountains, and all its hills, and all its valleys, and all its deserts, and all its trees, and all its herbs, and all its creeping things, and all its beasts, and all its cattle, and all its birds, and all its fish, and all human beings, and all their souls, and all their spirits, and all their breaths—You created everything for Your glory, and You created everything for Your service, and You created everything for Your fear, and You created everything to praise and to laud and to glorify and to exalt and to magnify and to sanctify and to bless Your great and awesome and holy and blessed name for ever and ever, Amen Selah."
12.3: When the hour arrives for the ministering angels to sing song (before the Holy One, blessed be He) Variant: A report of the singing angel, the Might and the Power dwells at the windows of the firmament of Harmon to hear and to harken to the voice of songs and melodies and praises ascending from the earth and from all the houses of assembly and from the houses of study and from all the Arabot of the firmament. And for what reason is He at the windows of the firmament of Harmon? Because the ministering angels have no permission to say song first above until Israel opens their mouths below and says: "The Lord our God," and afterward the angels say: "Holy," and "Holy," and "Blessed." When the angels call out in song and praise the name of the Holy One, blessed be He, what is the reason and appearance of "Holy, Holy, Holy"?
12.4: And how zealous is His name at that hour when the ministering angels hear at once together and say: "May the name of the Lord be blessed and praised now," and so they come from all the heavens of the firmament and all the windows and all the thin layers of the firmament, and firmament upon Arabot of the firmament, upon the Holy Living Creatures and the Ofanim of the earth and the wheels of splendor from the seven heavens of heavens—these are firmament after firmament, etc., and … properly according to the order of songs and melodies.
12.5: And these are the Kertot, those sparks of the rays from beneath His Throne of Glory, retinues upon retinues. And He established names, and pasturages, and kingdoms. Blessed are you, teachers of the To[rah] ; the merit of the Sabbath is yours, you who exalt the fathers. And all the host of the height made for them glory and greatness, the mighty ones of ATHeSaSh. Awake, the righteous one delights a little in the Lord God of Israel. They were still three; for it says: "Yours, O Lord, is the greatness and the power, etc." (1 Chron. 29:11), and it says: "How manifold are Your works, O Lord, etc." (Ps. 104:24). Therefore, how You shall be glorified, shall be exalted, shall be uplifted, O magnificent King; may You be blessed, may You be praised, may You be sanctified.
12.6: Tutrosiai Lord God of Israel (three times), who was called: Tutrosia, Tutrosiah, Potrosiah, Tutrosiah, Tutrosial, Tetrosig, Tutrosikh, Tutrosif, Tutrositz, Tutrosish, Tutrosib, Tutrosin, Tutrosis, Tutrosia, Tutrosiq, Tutrosit.
12.7: As for their form and their splendor, do not ask me, nor their interpretation; for it is a decree to know these great ones from Tutrosiai until Tutrosit. May this tradition be strengthened … Garpatz Shankhas Akat.

13.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: When Rabbi Akiva ben Ha-Kanah saw wicked Rome taking counsel against the mighty ones of Israel to destroy them, he stood and revealed the secret of the world—the measure which is like one who is worthy of beholding the King and His throne in His splendor and His beauty, and the Holy Living Creatures like Cherubim of Power and like the Ophannim of the Shekhinah, like a startled lightning bolt in the awesome Hashmal, like the appearance of joy around His throne, like eagles; and with flames that prevail, igniting eagle to eagle, and their priest dwelled there.
13.2: And like a wind of radiance that raises every supreme stone that was covering and pulling all the chambers of the palace, the ornaments of the firmament, in the mists of the streams of Zimuria. The Prince of the Presence, the servant of Tutrosial, the Lord, is exceedingly fair. To what is this measure of the "Descenders to the Chariot" comparable? To a man who has a ladder inside his house, upon which he ascends and descends, and no creature prevents him. So it is for everyone who is pure clean and purged from idolatry, sexual immorality, bloodshed, evil speech, swearing by the Name, brazenness, baseless hatred, and all persecution and negative commandments.
13.3: Third Guardian. Rabbi Ishmael said: Tutrosiai Lord, God of Israel, said to me: "My master, son of Nahum, happy is he and happy is the soul of everyone who is clean and purged from these eight qualities, for which Tutrotbeial Lord and Surya His servant acknowledge them." 3. He descends and gazes upon the wondrous majesty and the strange order—the majesty of loftiness and the order of gehiyon [resplendence]—which surges before His Throne of Glory three times every single day on high, from the day 2. the world was created until now; when Tutrosiai Lord comes, He conducts Himself by it on high.

14.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: As soon as my ears heard this Torah, my strength failed. I said to him, to Rabbi Nehunia ben Ha-Kanah: "Master, if so, there is no end to the matter, for there is no creature named 'Son of Shakkai' who is clean and purged from these eight qualities." He said to me: "Son of Nahum, if not, stand and bring before me all the mighty ones of the company and all the nobles of the academy, and I shall say before them the hidden and suppressed secrets—the wonders of the weaving of the web, of the perfection of the perfect, and its curling [arrangement] upon which it stands, and the axis of heaven and earth, to which all the wings of the earth and the world and the wings of the high firmament are tied, sewn, and joined, hanging and fastened to it; and the path of the ladder of the height, one end of which is on the earth and the other end on the right leg of the Throne of Glory."
14.2: 2. Rabbi Ishmael said: Immediately I stood and assembled all the Great Sanhedrin and all the Small Sanhedrin at the third alleyway which is in the House of the Lord. And he was sitting on a bench of pure marble which my father Elisha had given him from the property of my mother, for it was hers, which she had brought to him in her marriage contract.
14.3: 3. And Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel came, and Rabbi Eleazar the Great, and Rabbi Eleazar ben Dama, and Rabbi Eleazar ben Shammua, and Yochanan ben Dahabai, and Hananiah ben Hakinai, and Jonathan ben Uzziel, and Rabbi Akiva, and Rabbi Judah ben Bava. We came and sat before him, and the Palace of the Kind The companions were standing on their feet, for the heirs were sitting; fire and torches of fire and light intervened between them and them. And Rabbi Nehunia ben Ha-Kanah was sitting and arranging all the matters of the Merkabah, the descent and the ascent: how he who descends descends, and how he who ascends ascends. And when a man sought to descend to the Merkabah, he would call to Surya, Prince of the Presence, and adjure him one hundred and seventy-eight times by Tutrosiai Lord, who was called Tutrosi, Olatak, Tutrebeal, Topgar, Ashrunili, Ayu, Bohiel, and Nahadiril, Tatiel, and Shakhuziai, Rahvilon, Adiriron, and Adiririlon, the Lord God of Israel; [decreeing] that he should not add to one hundred and eighty times, nor should he diminish from them. If he added or subtracted, he would be shaken in his head at that time. Rather, his mouth should utter the names and the fingers of his hands count one hundred and twelve, and he masters the Merkabah.

15.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Rabbi Nehunia ben Ha-Kanah, my master, said: In seven palaces sits Tutrosiai, YHVH God of Israel, chamber within chamber, chamber within chamber. and at the entrance of each and every palace are eight gatekeepers: four to the right of the lintel and four to the left of the lintel.
15.2: 2. These are the names of the gatekeepers of the first palace: Dehaviel and Kashriel, Gaharriel and Kuziel, Tupriel and Dahariel, Matkiel and Shival.
15.3: 3. These are the names of the gatekeepers of the second palace: Tagriel and Matkiel, Tarhiel and Shaphiel, Shadriel and Satriel, Raashiel and Sahakiel.
15.4: 4. These are the names of the gatekeepers of the third palace: Shavriel and Ratsetsiel, Sharphiel and Salmiel, Saviel and Nahaviel, Hadraziel and Kurriel.
15.5: 5. These are the names of the gatekeepers of the fourth palace: Pahadiel and Gevurtiel, Kanziel and Shatkiel, Shatkiel and Arvael, and Kaphiel and Shaphiel.
15.6: 6. These are the names of the gatekeepers of the fifth palace: Tehalliel and Azriel, Natahiel and Mashuriel, Narphiel and Gadiel, Hadiel and Paltiel. and Paltiel—three. These are the names of the gatekeepers of the entrance of the sixth palace: Dumiel, Katspiel, Gadiel, Arsakdasbeal, Azrumiel, Parzael, Chakakiel, and Azrael—eight. At the entrance of the seventh palace stand gatekeepers, all of them mighty, tyrannical, fierce and hard, awesome and terrifying. They are taller than the mountains and sharper than the hills; their bows are drawn and held before them, and their swords are sharpened and held in their hands. Lightnings strike and sparks [fly] from above their eyes; jets of fire issue from their nostrils and torches of coal from their mouths. They are adorned with helmets and coats of mail, and spears and lances are suspended upon their arms.

16.1: Their horses are horses of darkness, horses of the shadow of death, horses of gloom, horses of fire, horses of blood, horses of hail, horses of iron, horses of mist, horses of storm, upon which are mounted those who stand by the Throne of Fire. They are full of broom-coals and they eat coals from the vessels, in the measure of forty se’ah of coals in a single mouth. The measure of the mouth of each and every horse is like the measure of three mangers of Caesarea. And there was fire within the vessels; and each and every horse drinks according to the full measure of a water-conduit like the Kidron stream, which carries and holds all the rainwater of all Jerusalem. And there was a cloud above their heads which distilled blood upon their heads and upon [the heads of] their horses. Such was the appearance and the measure of the gatekeepers of the entrance of the seventh palace. And between every entrance of every palace [were] three. And all the descenders to the Merkabah would ascend and not be harmed; rather, they would see all this host and descend in peace, coming to testify and recount the awesome and terrifying vision, which is not the case in any of the palaces of kings of flesh and blood. And they bless, praise, laud, glorify, exalt, and honor, giving glory, splendor, and greatness to Tutrosiai YHVH God of Israel, who rejoices in the descenders to the Merkabah and sits and waits for each and every one of Israel [to see] when he will descend and look upon the Majesty.
16.2: With wondrous pride and extraordinary dominion, with pride of loftiness and dominion of majesty that is stirred before the Throne of His Glory three times each and every day from on high, from the day the world was created until now, for His Name: Triple King, Upright King, Faithful King, Beloved King, Desired King, Supporting King, Humble King, Righteous King, Pious King, Holy King, Pure King, Blessed King, Proud King, Mighty King, Gracious King, Merciful King, King of kings of kings and Lord of lords. YHWH was the Delight, and enwrapped in Tutrusia’i YHWH, God of Israel; the consolation that He wraps for the day of redemption and the time of salvation, which is guarded for Israel after the destruction of the Last House. When will he descend—he who descends to the Merkabah? When will he see the pride of the heights? When will he hear the end and the time he will see the end of salvation of salvation? When will he see that which no eye has seen—salvation—and tell it to the seed of Abraham my beloved?

17.1: Said Rabbi Ishmael: When you come and stand at the entrance of the First Palace, take two seals in your two hands—one of Tutrusia’i YHWH and one of Suria, the Prince of the Presence of Tutrusia’i YHWH. Show those to those standing to the right, and the seal of Suria, the Prince of the Presence, show to those standing to the left. Immediately, Rachaviel the Prince—who is the head of the entrance of the First Palace and is appointed over the First Palace and stands at the right of the doorpost—and Tofia’el the Prince, who stands at the left of the doorpost with him, immediately take hold of you, one from your right and one from your left, until they lead you and deliver you over to Tagriel the Prince—who is the head of the entrance of the Second Palace and stands at the right of the doorpost—and Matfiel the Prince, who stands at the left of the doorpost with him. And show them those two seals: one of Adririon YHWH and one of Uzahia, the Prince of the Presence. Show Adririon YHWH to those standing to the left, and that of Uzahia, the Prince of the Presence, show to those standing to the left. Immediately they take hold of you, one from your right and one from your left, until they lead you and deliver you and hand you over and commend you to Shavuriel the Prince, who is the head of the entrance of the Third Palace and stands at the right of the doorpost, and Raziel the Prince, who stands at the left of the doorpost with him.
17.2: 3. And show them two seals: one of Zortek YHWH and one of Dahaviron, Prince of the Presence, of Artan YHWH. Show the one of Zortek to those standing to the right, and that of Dahaviron, Prince of the Presence, show to those standing to the left. Immediately they seize you, one from your right and one from your left, and two princes walk before you and two princes behind you, until they lead you and hand you over and commend you to Pazriel the Prince, who is the head of the entrance of the Fourth Palace and stands at the right of the doorpost, and Gevurtiel the Prince, who stands at the left of the doorpost with him.
17.3: 4. And show them two seals: one of Gevuriel YHWH and one of Marnizual, Prince of the Presence. Show the one of Gevuriel YHWH to those standing to the right, and that of Marnizual, Prince of the Presence, show to those standing to the left. Immediately they seize you, one from your right and one from your left, until they lead you and deliver you and hand you over and commend you to Netahel the Prince, who is the head of the entrance of the Fifth Palace and stands at the right of the doorpost, and Sharriel the Prince, who stands at the left of the doorpost with him.
17.4: 5. And show them two seals: one of Turtavia YHWH and one of Zehafnurya, Prince of the Presence. Show the one of Turtavia YHWH to those standing to the right, and that of Zehafnurya, Prince of the Presence, show to those standing to the left. Immediately they seize you and lead you—three princes before you and three princes behind you.
17.5: And perhaps 6. For the guards of the entrance of the Sixth Palace would destroy those who descend to the Merkabah—even the beloved of the Merkabah—who descend without permission. They would glare at them and strike them and burn them, and station others in their place. And even the subsequent ones who stand there, such is their nature: they are not afraid and it does not enter their hearts to say, "Why are we [standing here to be destroyed?]"
17.6: Seraphim—and indeed, what was it for us, that they do not destroy [those] of the descenders to the Merkabah, but not [those] among the descenders to the Merkabah [who are] without permission? And still, such is the manner of the guards of the entrance of the Sixth Palace.

18.1: 1. R. Ishmael said: The entire company said to me: You are a son of miracles, for you rule over the great light, the light of the Torah. Since Nehunia ben ha-Kanah—we see him returning and sitting among us—let us set [him] up, for he gazes into the vision of the Merkabah, and let him tell us: who are they, "from those who descend to the Merkabah and yet not among those who descend to the Merkabah," whom the guards of the entrance of the Sixth Palace would encounter, yet they would not oppress the descenders to the Merkabah at all? What is the difference between this one and that one?
18.2: 2. R. Ishmael said: Immediately I took a cloth of polat meaning it is purta, and I gave it to R. Akiba, and R. Akiba gave it to the sixth servant—he gave it to a slave so as not to tell you—and he placed this cloth near a woman who had immersed herself but the immersion was not effective for her. And the immersion [was such] that if that woman should come and state the measures of her menstrual period before the company, it is known that one prohibits meaning the last and the majority permit. And when [the impurity] of that woman was caught in this cloth, like the tip of your middle finger upon it, they said to her: "Do not press the tip of your middle finger upon it, but like a man who removes a scab that has fallen on him and pushes it away with a deceptive touch."
18.3: 3. They went and did so, and they struck the cloth before R. Ishmael, which was still [damp] from the vapor of the blood, full of palyaton oil that they had soaked in good balsam. And they struck it upon the knees of R. Nehunia ben ha-Kanah, and immediately they dismissed him from before the Throne of Glory where he had been sitting and seeing with wondrous pride and extraordinary dominion, in a stature of loftiness and majesty that is exalted before the Throne of Glory three times every single day on high, from the day the world was created until now, in praise.
18.4: 4. He was asked: "Who is he from those who descend to the Merkabah and yet not among those who descend to the Merkabah? Let him tell us." [He said]: "These are the people whom the descenders to the Merkabah take and place above themselves and seat them … " them before them and says to them: "Observe and see, listen and write all that I say and all that we hear from before the Throne of Glory." And those people were not careful in this; therefore the guards of the entrance of the Sixth Palace would strike them.
18.5: Be careful to select for yourselves worthy men, and they are the joiners of the lightning-flashes. O Lord, when you come and stand at the entrance of the Sixth Palace, show three seals to the guards of the entrance of the Sixth Palace.
18.6: The seal for Qatspiel the Prince, whose sword was drawn in his hand, and flashes of lightning were flashing and issuing from it, and he would stir [wrath] against anyone who is not worthy to look upon the King and His Throne, and there is no creature that can restrain his hand. And his sword was screaming and saying: "Woe and destruction!" at the right doorpost .
18.7: One [seal] is found for Dumiel. And is Dumiel indeed his name? Is not his name A.B.G. A.B.Y. Avigatidihas? Why then is his name called Dumiel? R. Ishmael said: Thus did R. Akiba ben ha-Kanah, my master, say to me: Every single day a divine voice goes out from the Arabot of the firmament and proclaims and says, "The Glory of the heights." Thus it said: Tapus u-Var Ma'anyah u-Peninei She'ateyah, the God of Israel—call him Dumiel after My name: just as I see and remain silent (maharish), so too Dumiel. His authority is at the right doorpost. And Qatspiel the Prince would push them [the unworthy], yet he has neither enmity nor rivalry toward him, but rather these are for My glory and those are for My glory.

19.1: And Hadriel and Pa'ali Pa'ali—show these two seals to the one who belongs to Qatspiel, and with knowledge show [them] to Dumiel the Prince, the upright and humble prince. Immediately Qatspiel the Prince would draw his bow and whet his sword, and bring a storm wind for you, and seat you in a carriage of cloud. And he would blast before you the measure of six thousand horns, and thirty thousand myriad shofars, and forty thousand myriad trumpets. And Dumiel the Prince takes a gift and goes before you. (2) And what is the gift? R. Ishmael said: Thus said R. Akiba ben ha-Kanah, my master: This gift that Dumiel the Prince [one] takes hold of before the carriage of a person who is worthy and descends to the Chariot. It is not a gift of silver, nor is it a gift of gold; rather, they would praise that person. And they would not question him—neither in the first Palace, nor in the second Palace, nor in the third Palace, nor in the fourth Palace, nor in the fifth Palace, nor in the sixth Palace, nor in the seventh Palace. Rather, he shows them seals, and they let him pass let him pass, and he enters. And at the entrance of the sixth Palace was Dumiel the Prince, the guardian of the entrance on the right of the entrance of the sixth Palace; he sits upon a bench on the right made of pure white stone, in which is the brilliance of the lights of the firmament, and the cushion of the world is Adaspan, and in an inscription upon it was extended "Y-H-W-H, God of Israel." And Dumiel the Prince would receive him with a gracious countenance and seat him upon a bench of pure white stone, and sit beside him on his right.

20.1: And he would say to him: "Two [matters] to exempt even from the destroyer and the intermingler." Thus, the one who descends does not descend to the Chariot unless he possesses these two attributes: Torah, Prophets, and Writings; and he repeats Mishnah, Midrash, Halakhot, and Aggadot, and their explanation—the laws of the forbidden and the permitted; and one who has fulfilled every negative commandment written in the Torah and keeps all the warnings of statutes and judgments and of the laws that were told to Moses from Sinai. When he said to Dumiel the Prince, "I possess one of these two attributes," Dumiel the Prince would attend to Gabriel the Scribe, and he would write the document for him and hang the document upon the frame of that person's carriage, to say: "Such and such is the Torah of so-and-so, and such and such are his deeds, and he seeks to enter before the Throne of Glory."
20.2: And as soon as the guards of the entrance of the seventh Palace would see Dumiel and Gabriel and Qanfiel approaching before the carriage of that person who is worthy and descends to the Chariot, they cover their faces and sit as those rebuked and silenced; they unstring the bent bows and return the whetted swords to their sheaths. Nevertheless, he must show them a great seal and a fearsome crown, [proclaiming] that the man is remembered from the Dwelling, and when Y-H-W-H God of Israel extended Israel: and they would gaze before the Throne of Glory, and all kinds of gracious melodies of music and song would tremble before Him, and they would come before Him until they raise him and seat him beside the Cherubim, beside the Ophanim, and beside the Holy Living Creatures. And he beholds wonders and mighty deeds, majesty and greatness, holiness and purity, awe, humility, and rectitude. At that hour, Rabbi Ishmael said: Happy are all the Companions regarding this measure; it is like a man who has a ladder within his house, such that he ascends and descends and no creature restrains him—this is according to the measure of the Knower of Secrets and the Master of Mysteries.

21.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: At the hour that Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel [spoke], he said to him: In a mere moment Nof Ke … and the Pagurai, and He made us kings like a simple steward. What has happened to you, that this judgment was exacted against us? Do you think that the son of Shuzal is known? He is a small man in Israel; and what if he descended plainly and came and stood at the entrance of the Seventh Palace?
21.2: Rabbi Ishmael said: I went and entered before the words of Hezekiah ben Hiku, the Prince of the Chariot, and he said: Let Him not be angry with me—why [did you seek] the words of life? He said to him: Thus it is pleasant. If so, what is My honor among you? You have set in your mouths Torah, Prophets, and Writings, Mishnah, Midrash, Halakhot, and Aggadot, and the interpretation of the laws of the forbidden and the permitted. Were it not for the secrets of the Torah that I [concealed] from you, would you have shown such pride and greatness before Me? I know for what reason you came; you came only concerning the guards of the entrance of the Seventh Palace.
21.3: Go and say to the Prince: To all the guards of the entrances of the six Palaces there is permission to mention the names of each and every one of them and to touch them; but as for the guards of the entrance of the Seventh Palace, the report of them terrifies a man, and he cannot touch them, because each and every one of them is called by the name of the King of the World. I have not explained them now that you say to me, "Explain." Come and stand on your feet, and each and every one of you, as he hears came forth from his mouth, for it is strong and jubilant before you; and perhaps, and immediately, all the heroes of the company and all the nobles of the academy came and stood upon their feet before him. They were strengthened—thus the Holy One, Blessed be He—and he speaks, and they fall upon their faces, and the deniers write.

22.1: These are the names of the guards of the entrance of the Seventh Palace: Vahapnuria’i, the Lord, God of Israel, a glorious and delightful prince, mighty and proud; the Lord, a glorious, delightful, and awesome prince; Atriniel, the Lord, a glorious, delightful, awesome, and terrifying prince; Kadniel, the Lord, a glorious, delightful, awesome, and terrifying prince; and Vahapnuria’i, the Lord, a glorious and delightful prince; Akhirzyahi, the Lord, a glorious, delightful, and awesome prince; Atriniel, the Lord, a glorious, delightful, awesome, and terrifying prince; Kadniel, the Lord, a glorious, delightful, awesome, and terrifying prince; and the precious and magnificent Azriel, the Lord, a glorious, delightful, awesome, terrifying, precious, and magnificent prince; and the mighty Patuniel, the Lord, a glorious, delightful, awesome, terrifying, precious, and magnificent prince; and the mighty and noble Anaphiel, the Lord, the prince whose name is mentioned before the Glory three times every single day from the day the world was created for praise. For what reason? Because the signet ring of the seal of heaven and earth is delivered into his hand . And when all who are on high see him, they kneel and fall and prostrate before him, which is not the case [elsewhere] on high.
22.2: And if you should say: Before the Prince of the Presence they do not fall—except for the eight before the Throne of Glory—for they do not prostrate to the Prince of the Presence; yet before Anaphiel they do prostrate by permission and by will. Asher Ve-Sarev Ve-Gag Ya Pumiel, may His name be praised, according to the will of the Lord, God of Israel. These are the names of the guards of the entrance of the Seventh Palace of the Descent: n. The distinction of the names of the Ascent: Anaphiel, the Lord, a glorious, delightful, and awesome prince who was called Akhirzyahi, the Lord; Dalkiel, the Lord, a glorious, delightful, and awesome prince who was called Lekakhpriel, the Lord; and Hakdiel, the Lord, a glorious, delightful, and awesome prince who was called Atriniel, the Lord; Yashishiel, the Lord, a glorious, delightful, and awesome prince who was called Kanual, the Lord; Nurpaniel Nuriel, the Lord, a glorious, delightful, and awesome prince, who used to be called Shaqdiel. The Lord, Azriel, the Lord, a glorious, delightful, and awesome prince, who used to be called Haliel. The Lord, Azfiel, a glorious, delightful, awesome, terrifying, precious, magnificent, mighty, majestic, strong, upright, and brave prince, who used to be called Tofriel. The Lord, 7. And why was his name called Azfiel?
22.3: Because of the branch of the crowns of crowns that was placed upon his head, which shielded and covered all the chambers of the Palace of Arabot of the Firmament, like the Creator of the Beginning. Just as concerning the Creator of the Beginning it is written, "the appearance of the throne of heaven is His majesty," so too Azfiel the prince serves as an agent in the name of his Master. And why is he beloved and honored above all the guards of the entrances of the Palaces? Because he refined his conduct he opened the entrance of the Seventh Palace and closed it before the Throne of Glory; for he refined his conduct and guarded until the entrance of the Seventh Palace. And the Holy Living Creatures are until the entrance of the Seventh Palace, and the Cherubim and the Ophanim are until the entrance of the Seventh Palace. And one hundred and two hundred and fifty-six lanterns in every Holy Living Creature until the entrance of the Seventh Palace. 8. Greater than all of them: five hundred and seventy eyes there are in the four Holy Living Creatures until the entrance of the Seventh Palace, which are of the form of faces; faces of sixteen—sixteen faces there are in every creature until the entrance of the Seventh Palace.

23.1: And when a man sought to descend to the Chariot, Azfiel the prince would open for him the doors of the entrance of the Seventh Palace, and that man would enter and stand upon the threshold of the entrance of the Seventh Palace. And the Holy Living Creatures would cast upon him five hundred and seventy eyes, and every single eye of the six Holy Living Creatures is fixed as the measure of a large sieve of the discerning, and the appearance of their eyes is like lightning flashes running to and fro—except for a little [like] a large Cherub—and the Ophanim of the Shekhinah, which are like torches of light and like the flames of coals of broom-wood. 9. And that man would tremble and be shaken, and recoil and be terrified, dismayed, fainting and falling backward. And Azfiel the prince would support him—he and the sixty-three guards of the entrances of the seven Palaces.
23.2: And they would all respond to him and say to him: “Fear not, son of the beloved seed. Enter and behold the King in His beauty; as long as you bow down, you shall not be burned.” 3. He is an upright King, He is a faithful King, He is a humble King, a poor King, He is a righteous King, He is a pious King, He is a holy King, He is a pure King, He is a blessed King, He is a proud King, He is a mighty King, He is a gracious King, He is a merciful King, He is a lowly King, a lowly King is He. 3. And they would immediately grant him strength, and a horn was sounded from above the firmament that was over their heads. The Holy Living Creatures cover their faces, and the Cherubim and the Ophanim turn their faces away; and he enters and stands before the Throne of Glory.

24.2: Once he stood before the Throne of Glory, he opened [his mouth] and spoke a song. The Throne of Glory sings every single day: praise, song, melody, blessing, and thanksgiving; laudation, hallelujah, and glorification; thanks and acknowledgments; the sprouting of the horn, redemption, rejoicing, exultation, joy, and gladness; singing, pleasantness, habitation, beauty, truth, righteousness, and uprightness; treasure, splendor, and strength; peace, tranquility, ease, and the serenity of rest and consolation; quietude, silence, and peace; security, trust, and goodness; love, desire, grace, and lovingkindness; beauty, form, majesty, and compassion; radiance, brightness, merit, and shining; appearance, the measurement of the body, light, branch, and diadem; wonders and salvation; distant, seasoned, and the luminary of excellencies; exhilaration, dread, power, height, and preciousness; strength, dominion, and might; matters of exaltation, majesty, strength, might, and valor; holiness, purity, and cleanness; great pride and sovereignty; majesty and splendor, glory and beauty—to bring forth the LORD, God of Israel. 2. A glorified King, wrapped in splendor, adorned with the ornaments of song; like the majesty of glory and the beauty of the crown of pride and the diadem of awesomeness. His name is pleasant to Him, and His memory supports Him; His throne is glorified by Him, and His palace is adorned for Him; His glory is desired by Him, and His majesty is fitting for Him; His strength is pleasant to Him, and those who study His [Torah] make the song and the uprightness of His mighty power pleasant for Him. 3.
24.3: 3. King of the kings of kings, God of gods, and Lord of lords; exalted by the bindings of crowns, surrounded by clouds of brilliant light; within the clouds of His majesty is the Throne of Heaven, and in His splendor is the beauty of the celestial heights; and from His beauty the depths are kindled, and from His appearance the skies are laid bare, and their dwellings tremble from the fear of His appearance. And their strength is shaken, our crown; and the precious ones have stirred His portion, and all trees shall rejoice; at His word the grasses sing in His joy, and at His word the heavens stand; and the precious ones go forth in flames of fire. Freedom He gave to their seekers, and tranquility to those who uphold them. 3. A King beloved, desirable, and pure; rising above the kings and graceful; rising above the proud, majestic; exalting Himself above the mighty and rising above the awesome ones; the pride of kings, the praise for the noble ones, a treasure for the holy, peace for the wretched; whose palms are open to those who call Him, sweet to those who hope for Him. His name is righteous in all His ways, upright in all His deeds, pure in all His attributes, clear in counsel and at every moment, lucid in understanding and action; Witness to every matter, Judge for every soul, Arbiter in every measure; recognized in wisdom and in every secret, mighty in holiness and in purity.
24.4: The LORD is a King of truth, unique; a King who brings death and gives life; a King who lives and endures forever; a King who speaks and acts, and sustains all; a King who forms everything, who strikes and creates every healing; a King who makes all evil and prepares all good; a King who nourishes all His works, nourishes and sustains all His creatures; a King high and lowly, to every humble and to every courageous one, He is strong.

25.1: A King high and exalted, lofty and wonderful, beloved and joyful, upright and faithful, precious and honored, strong and courageous, righteous and true, holy and pure, pious, great, and mighty. 3. His name is mighty, precious, awesome, and terrifying; sitting upon a throne high and exalted; strength, power, might, preciousness, awesome and terrifying; paved upon His path, graceful, established upon crowns of splendor in the chambers of the palace of pride. Strength, power, preciousness, awesome, mighty and terrifying; He sees into the depths, gazes into the hidden places, beholds the thoughts; Master of the place—there He is, His name alone. salvation and His desire is not to exchange nor to retract His words, nor to delay His will. There is no place to flee from Him, and no hiding or concealing oneself from His presence. 3. He who shall reign forever shall reign over you for generation to generation. A King merciful and gracious, pardoning and forgiving deeds and passing over [transgression].
25.2: You are glorified upon the palace of pride; You are exalted in all pleasantness; You are beautified in every song; You are uplifted above those crowned with splendor; You are powerful in all deeds; You are majestic over all creatures; You are honored upon Your throne of glory; You are sanctified upon all Your delight; You are blessed with every blessing; You are praised with all praises; You are lauded with every glorification; You are extolled with all shouts of joy; You are magnified and their peace; You are sanctified, Shaddai, unto the delights of Sa’ay YYY. 4. King of all perfect ones, Lord of all deeds, wise in all secrets, ruler in all generations, one God who is from everlasting, who is for forever and ever, Selah. 5. And I saw as the color of the chashmal; it was flashing and standing. And regarding those who descend to the Chariot: whether one who is worthy to descend to the Chariot or one who is not worthy to descend to the Chariot. If he was worthy to descend to the Chariot, when they say to him, "Enter," and he does not enter, they say to him again, "Enter," and immediately he enters. They would praise him and say: "Blessed be the Lord of the descenders to the Chariot." But if he is not worthy to descend to the Chariot, as soon as they say to him, "Do not enter," and he enters, they immediately cast upon him brands of iron. 6.
25.3: Because the guardians of the gate of the sixth palace cast and throw upon him a million vessels of water, yet there is not even a single drop there. And if he said, "What is the nature of these waters?" immediately they run after him to stone him, saying to him: "Empty one! Perhaps you are of the seed of those who kissed the calf, and you are not worthy to see the King and His throne." If it is so, a divine voice goes forth from the Aravot firmament and says: "Well have you spoken! He is of the seed of those who kissed the calf, and he is not worthy to see the King and His throne." He does not move from there until they cast upon him a million brands of iron. 7. Michael, the Glory of the LORD God of Israel, Master of mighty deeds. Before You, LORD God of Israel, they shall bow They shall kneel and prostrate themselves before you, and the Lord, God of Israel, shall be exalted. The heavens shall be majestic and shall utter songs of joy before the Lord, God of Israel. They shall praise the throne of Your glory, and unto You shall He give majesty and abundance of strength and beauty before the Lord, God of Israel. Your ministers shall crown You with crowns and sing to You a new song; they shall be fulfilled by Your likeness forever, and You shall be One for ever and ever.
25.4: Before You they shall bless, before You they shall praise, before You they shall glorify, before You they shall exalt, before You they shall give thanks, for You are the Lord, God of Israel, mighty in valor and abundant in salvation; the Rock, God, Wise in secrets and Master of hidden things .

26.1: You are the worker of mighty deeds, renewing Your creatures every single day. Every day a hundred new ones arise to exalt Your praise. Pure and radiant splendor shines amidst myriads of fire, a glowing light. He who despises hatred and jealousy, who distances enmity and strife, who removes anger, who takes away wrath. The Chariot is all grace and goodness. Your Cherubim of glory are a rising fire upon Cherubim of fire, upon—upon the Princes, the Seraphim, Seraphim of flame; they stand around His throne, calling out one to another: "Extol Him who rides upon the clouds," with praise and laud, a song of thanksgiving and acknowledgments, praise, beauty, and the whisper of acclaim, majesty and kindness; to glorify, to recognize, to strengthen, to bless, to examine, to choose the Mighty One—seemly and exalted. In their mouths is melody, on their tongues are songs of joy. They have no slumber, neither by night nor by day, but only in the glowing light is melody and praise.
26.2: For You are the Great Lord, the Mighty and the Awesome, the Righteous, the Pious, the Holy, and the Faithful, slow to anger and abundant in kindness and truth. You are the Lord, God of gods and Lord of lords. You are Great; all those of greatness magnify You. You are Mighty; all those of might declare Your power. You are Awesome; all those of song raise their voices for You. You are Pious and Righteous; all those of righteousness declare You righteous. You are Pious; all those of piety hope for You. You are Holy; all those of holiness sanctify You. You are Faithful in Your words; all those of faith believe in You, for it was You who revealed Your secret to Moses and did not conceal it.
26.3: All Your mighty deeds—at the time when no speech issues from Your mouth, all the lofty mountains tremble and stand before You in great terror; at the time when speech issues from Your mouth, they are all consumed by flames of fire. You search the reins and choose the faithful. You dwell in the walking and in the sojourning; to Him, awake like the judgment of flames. You are the Mighty of the proud, exalted above all, triumphing over all, humbling the proud and exalting the humble; blessed be He.
26.4: The Lord is exalted among the creatures through man: the likeness of man You established in Your throne. You set the face of man for them, and the hands of man beneath their wings; the will of their countenances labor like man, kneeling and prostrating like man; His throne and Your dread, O King, are upon them.
26.5: Exalted among the beasts is the ox: the likeness of an ox You established in Your throne. The will of the ox, laboring like the ox, they stand upon his station; and Your dread, O Holy One, is upon them.
26.6: Exalted among the wild animals is the lion: the likeness of a lion You established in the throne. They roar like a lion, and Your dread is like a lion, and the blast of His strength is like a lion; and Your dread, O Lion, is upon them.
26.7: Exalted among the birds is the eagle: the likeness of an eagle You established in the throne. They run like an eagle, they are swift as an eagle, they fly like an eagle and soar like an eagle; and Your dread, O Pure One, is upon them. And all of them declare Your holiness threefold, with a threefold sanctification, as it is said: Holy, Holy, Holy.
26.8: May You be magnified, be glorified, be exalted, be uplifted, be beautified, be blessed, be praised, be extolled, be elevated, be sanctified, be raised, and be lauded; for it is the duty of all creatures before You to give thanks, to exalt, to praise, to bless, to beautify, to laud, to magnify, to sanctify, to sing, and to give strength, and to acclaim You, the Great and Holy King, Ruler over the upper and the lower realms, over the first and the last; for from within the movement and the trembling, the ministers declare Your holiness threefold, with a threefold sanctification, as it is said: Holy, Holy, Holy.
26.9: The Majesty and the Faithfulness belong to Him who lives eternally. The Understanding and the Blessing belong to Him who lives eternally. The Greatness and the Might belong to Him who lives eternally. The Knowledge and the Speech belong to Him who lives eternally. The Splendor and the Beauty belong to Him who lives eternally. The Rectitude and the Enduring-Faithfulness belong to Him who lives eternally. The Merit and the Memory belong to Him who lives eternally. The Grace and the Kindness belong to Him who lives eternally.
26.10: Perfections, Purity, and Goodness—to the Life of the Worlds. The Honor and the Salvation—to the Life of the Worlds. The Crown and the Glory—to the Life of the Worlds. The Instruction and the Heartening—to the Life of the Worlds. The Kingdom and the Dominion—to the Life of the Worlds. The Beauty and the Eternity—to the Life of the Worlds. The Secret and the Intellect—to the Life of the Worlds. The Strength and the Humility—to the Life of the Worlds. The Splendor and the Wonder—to the Life of the Worlds. The Righteousness and the Charity—to the Life of the Worlds. The Sanctification and the Holiness—to the Life of the Worlds. The Serenity and the Quiet—to the Life of the Worlds. The Praise and the Beauty—to the Life of the Worlds.
26.11: Who can speak of one of the thousand thousands and the multitude of myriads of Your mighty deeds, King of kings of kings, blessed be He? For the living creatures (Chayyot) serve and prostrate themselves before You in a still small voice. They are fire, their movement is fire, and their speech is fire; and they are reflected as fire from before the fire, lest they be consumed by the flames of fire surrounding You. To You we have encompassed, to You the Te’ofes has affirmed in the preciousness of the Hinus. Mystery and intellect, girded with power, wrapped in majesty; no eye can behold where Your dwelling is, Great and Holy King, Ruler over the upper and the lower beings, over the first and the last. There is none, neither among the upper nor the lower, neither among the first nor the last, who is able to know Your works and to search out all Your wonders. Just as one cannot compare Aleph to Aleph, Bet to Bet, Gimel to Gimel, Dalet to Dalet, He to He, Vav to Vav, Zayin to Zayin, Het to Het.
26.12: Metatron, whose name is called after the Name: Mikhniael is his name; Ziviel is his name; Ayayah is his name; Yehoviel is his name; Mivael is his name; Snusniel is his name; Sansanoyria is his name. And out of the love with which they loved him on high, they would call him in the holy camps: "Metatron, servant of the Lord." Slow to anger and great in kindness; Blessed art Thou, O Lord, Wise of the Mysteries and Master of Secrets. Amen and Amen.
26.13: Finished is the Order of the Three Gates of the Chariot (Merkabah).
26.14: Completed are the Laws of the Palaces (Hekhalot)

1.2: Rabbi Ishmael said: Thus spoke Rabbi Akiva in the name of Rabbi Eliezer the Great: From the day that the Torah was given to Israel until the Last House was built, the Torah was given; but its majesty and its preciousness, its glory and its greatness, and its beauty, its awe, its dread, and its fear, its wealth and its majesty, and its pride, the sweat and the quaking and the trembling, the strength and the power of its dominion and its might were not given until the Last House was built, and the Shekhinah did not dwell within it.
1.3: 2. Israel stood to pour out a complaint before their Father in heaven, saying: "You have cast many troubles upon us; it cannot be endured and it cannot be abandoned. You have cast upon us our yoke and a heavy burden. You said to us: 'Build for Me a house,' and even though you are building, 'Occupy yourselves with the Torah and with the repentance of My children.'" [God said:] "A broken and nullified thing and greatness was yours among the exiles, and you were longing: 'When shall I hear the sound of the words of My Torah from your mouths?' For you did not act rightly, and I did not act rightly. You did not act rightly, for you rebelled against Me and brought wrath upon yourselves; and I arose and brought about destruction and desolation upon My city, and upon My house, and upon My children. And I also did not act rightly, for I stood against you and sealed against you a decree of judgment that is certainly bitter, which stands forever and for all eternity. Let there be a dispute for it—a measure that has no length, but is either a year or two or ten or thirty, and if by strength, a hundred, and then it passes away. Rather, you have reproved Me well, for you have obeyed; I have already accepted your reproof upon Myself."
1.4: 4. "For the grace of Israel has been arranged before Me, and the sorrow of the Torah has covered Me." They pleaded with those words and they were accepted by Me. They said, "Be appeased; occupy yourselves with the House of My choosing, and the Torah shall not depart from your mouths. For I am the Master of Wonders and the Lord of Marvels; mighty deeds stir before Him, which are [ineffable] and wonders before My throne. And who has preceded Me, that I should repay him? Who has called Me and I did not answer immediately?" They said before Him all your requests.
1.5: Your requests and your soul’s desire are upon Me, for in My mouth and the mouths of My companions nothing is lacking in them. State your requests and they shall be granted to you, and your soul’s desire shall be fulfilled immediately. For as I live, at this very time next year—my soul [longed] until I saw you, and there is no time like this time, for your love has cleaved to my heart, and my heart recognized.

2.1: I know what you seek and what you long for. You seek abundant Torah, an abundance of Talmud, and a multitude of traditions to hear. Are you not wearying? You desire to increase a great multitude, to make testimony like mountains upon mountains, to distinguish wisdom like hills upon hills, to separate the Talmud into partitions and dialectics in the streets; to increase laws like the sand of the sea and many as the dust of the earth; to establish academies at the gates of the tents, to explain to them prohibition and permission, to declare impure that which is impure and to declare pure that which is pure, to declare fit that which is fit and to declare unfit that which is unfit, to distinguish between types of blood, to distinguish between types of blood; to instruct the generations what they should do, to tie crowns upon your heads and a royal diadem in your hand, to compel kings to bow down to you, to maintain your dominion so they bow before you; to proclaim your name under the whole vault of heaven and your renown in all the coastal cities; to make your faces shine like the rising of the day, and [the mark] between your eyes like the morning star.
2.2: If you merit this seal, to use the crown of the one who inherits the earth, no simpleton, fool, or dullard shall be found in your seat. You shall rejoice while the ministering angels are saddened. This is one of the secrets that issued from My storehouse: the voice of your academies shall be like clouds of incense—not through toil or weariness, but by the power of the name of this seal and the memory of the crown. The wonder wonders at you, and this likeness is upon you; many are perfected according to your excellence, and their fame goes out upon the fame of your glory. For wealth and riches shall prevail upon you, and the great ones of the world shall cleave to you; the family into which you marry shall be surrounded by noble lineage and strength.
2.3: The twofold [praise] of His servants: he who is blessed through you is blessed, and he who is praised through you is praised. Because of the preciousness of the many, you are called "those who bring merit to creatures"; [near] are you. The fixing of new months shall go forth from you, and because of the flavor of the cunning of your wisdom, [the Lord] shall be praised through you. By your word is the wisdom of the house of law, for you appoint Exilarchs and town judges; by your authority the ordinance of peace goes forth from you, and none disputes it. A great war was fought against Me by the ministers of the great Accuser, from the [ministering angels], etc. His response:

3.1: This secret shall not leave the house of Your treasuries, nor the hidden cunning from Your storehouses. Do not place flesh and blood like us [there]; do not liken other human beings in our stead. Have we not labored in the Torah as much as they labor? And from the [earliest] generations onward, they have fulfilled it with great toil and great burden. This is Your glory and this is Your splendor: when they praise, they return and give thanks before You; they call to You with a whole heart and supplicate: "May it be Your will that what we have acquired remain in our hands, and what we have studied be established in our hands. May our kidneys rectify what we have heard, and strengthen, O strengthen our hearts in the words of the Talmud we heard from the mouth of the Master, and let them honor one another." But if You reveal this secret to Your children, the small will be like the great, and the fool like the wise.
3.2: And this is the response of His servants to the ministers of God: "My servants, do not trouble Me in this matter. This secret has gone forth from the house of My treasuries and the hidden cunning from My storehouses. To a beloved people I reveal it; to a faithful seed I shall teach it. It was given from the days of old and from the days of creation, prepared for them forever. It did not enter My heart to give it to all those generations from the days of Moses until now; it was kept for this generation to use until the end of all generations. For they went from evil to evil and knew Me not, for their heart slipped from the heights, and the words of Torah were hard in their ears like copper and iron. For them, it is fitting to use it, to bring … "
3.3: 104 and servants … to bring Torah like water into their midst and like oil into their bones. For Israel was in My eyes [as] water against which My anger burned, and I struck, and the mountains were shattered, and their carcasses were like refuse in the midst of the streets. By what shall I know him? By what shall I comfort him? Or what goodly attribute of desire do I have on high that I might bring out and give to him and rejoice in him? I looked and saw: there is gold with Me, and there is gold in the world; silver with Me, and there is silver in the world; precious stones and pearls with Me, and there are precious stones and pearls in the world; wheat and barley, honey and oil I have already given to her. They stumbled; but what is missing from the world … and what is this that is not in the world? An attribute of splendor with which they may be beautified. Rabbi Ishmael said: Thus said Rabbi Akiva in the name of Rabbi Eliezer the Great: Our ancestors did not accept to place any stone of stone in the Temple of the Lord until they cleared [a place for] the King of the World and for all His ministers, and it was engraved for Him, and He revealed to them the Prince of the Torah: how they should make him, and how they should expound him, and how they should employ him. Immediately the Holy Spirit appeared, like the building of the Third [Temple] which is in the Third House of the Lord, for the Shekhinah had not descended nor dwelt in the Holy of Holies because of the decree.
3.4: When our ancestors saw the Throne of Glory depart and stand between the Porch and the Altar—for it had been dwelling [there] until that hour—at that they did not weep, except over the place of the forms, which are forms standing to serve upon them: the Porch, the Altar, the Sanctuary, and the entire House. And when our ancestors saw the Throne of Glory exalted from its midst, standing between the Porch and the Altar with the King of the World upon it, they immediately fell upon their faces and upon the latter [more] than the former at that hour he says: "The glory of this house shall be great" in measure. for in the First Temple they were not engraved … but by a voice: "This is for Me, and for My throne, and for all My ministers." [He said:] "Would that … why do you fall and cast yourselves upon your faces? Stand and sit before My throne according to the manner in which you sit in the academy." And they grasped the crown and received the seal and learned the order of this Prince of the Torah: how you shall make him, how you shall expound him, how you shall employ [him]. in it; for they would bring up clouds to wash, they were gazing [at] your heart in the Torah. Immediately, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel answered and stood on his feet before the angelic attendants, and he was expounding the names of the Prince of the Torah, one by its name, [which is] Saskanaz, and the name of the seal is Noa.

4.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Thus said Rabbi Akiva in the name of Rabbi Eliezer the Great: A man who takes hold of the [ritual of the] Prince of the Torah, this one shall wash his clothes and his garments, and immerse in a rigorous immersion [to remove] the doubt of an intervening substance [after] a seminal emission, and he shall enter and sit for twelve days in a room or in an upper chamber; let him not go out and let him not come in. He shall not eat and he shall not drink except from evening to evening, when he may eat his bread with a clean hand and drink pure water, and he shall not taste any kind of vegetable.
4.2: And he shall establish this study of the Prince of the Torah in prayer three times each day, after the prayer that he shall pray from its beginning to its end, and afterward he shall sit and repeat it in study for the twelve days, the days of his fasts, from morning until evening, and he shall not labor. And at every hour that he finishes, he shall stand on his feet and adjure the servants by their King, and call out twelve times to each and every Prince, and afterward he shall adjure him with the seal for each and every one of them.
4.3: And these are their names: Sheqadhuzyay the Lord [is] the Prince, and Happanoryay the Lord [is] the Prince, and Hobadiel the Lord [is] the Prince, Akhdriel the Lord [is] the Prince, and Happadriel the Lord [is] the Prince, and Hadarion the Lord [is] the Prince, and Zenubihay the Lord [is] the Prince, and Tarusyay the Lord [is] the Prince, and Shalniluhay the Lord [is] the Prince, Sanganai the Lord [is] the Prince, Palitrihu the Lord [is] the Prince, Dehibiron the Lord [is] the Prince, and Addiriron the Lord [is] the Prince. And he shall adjure them by the name of Ten: by the name of Yaphtiel, who is the glory of the height of the academies of his King; and by the name of Sarkiel, who is of the Princes of the Chariot; and by the name of Shahadriel, who is beloved; and by the name of Chasdiel, who is called for might, for six hours each day. Then he shall return and adjure them—the four latter Princes—with the Great Seal and with the great oath, by the name of Zeboni, which is a great seal. great, and the throne of His Torah that was sanctified, and the awesome crown of the Lord. And upon the completion of twelve days, he shall go out to all the measures of Torah that he seeks, whether for Scripture, or for Mishnah, or for Talmud, and even for the beholding of the Chariot; for in a measure of purity he goes out, and he is guarded and assisted. And there is joy, for the learning is in our hands—an ordinance of the ancients and a tradition of the old ones who wrote and told it to the generations, so that the humble may use it, and whoever is worthy may study them.

5.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Thus said Rabbi Akiva in the name of Rabbi Eliezer the Great: Happy is he whose fathers’ merit assists him and the righteousness of those who bore him stands for him, and let him serve with this crown and with this seal, and they shall be bound to him, and he shall take pride in the crown of Torah. 2 Rabbi Ishmael said: The matter was performed through Rabbi Eliezer and he was answered, but not everyone believed. It was performed again through me, and I did not believe until I brought a certain individual, and he became like me. It was performed again through the shepherds, and they became like me. They brought Rabbi Akiva down to the Diaspora, clad in linen, and he remained until it was performed through the many who had neither read nor studied, yet they studied and acted like disciples of the wise. 3 He came and confirmed and agreed to their testimony in the court of the Nasi M after this matter was performed even in the Diaspora and succeeded. And thus it was: Rabbi Eliezer the Great and the Sages were saying, "Perhaps by the merit of the Land of Israel it suffices for him," and they did not believe until they brought Rabbi Akiva down to Babylon, and it was performed and succeeded and he testified, and afterward we heard and rejoiced. 4 Rabbi Ishmael said: What should a man open with before he prays [the prayer] of this Torah? When he stands to pray, let him say: "May You be glorified, may You be exalted, may You be uplifted, O magnificent King."
5.2: Just as it is written in the chapter of the seven, and he says: "Who would not exalt You, O awesome and terrifying King of all Your ministers? In trembling and in quaking they minister to You; in terror and in shuddering they are terrified before You by the decree, for this is with one mouth—Your name is awesome." they find a little dread and awe in which they stand before You; there is no earlier and there is no later. And anyone who delays the voice from his fellow—that is to say, by the measure of a cubit of the measure—is pushed away, and a flaming fire pushes him, as it is said: "Holy," etc.

1.1: *Chapter of Rabbi Nehuniah ben Ha-Kanah, which he taught to Rabbi Ishmael*
1.2: Who can utter the mighty acts of the Lord, and who can declare the praise of the King of kings of kings? These are the ministering angels. May You be glorified, may You be praised, etc. Lord God of Israel, blessed is He forever, may You be exalted forever. Rabbi Ishmael said: For three years Rabbi Nehuniah ben Ha-Kanah saw me as a growing youth and as a growing sword; Scripture that I would read and repeat today, on the morrow I would forget. And when I saw that my learning was not sustained in my hand, I arose and restrained myself from eating and drinking, from washing and anointing, and from the use of the bed; and no word of song or chant issued from my mouth. Rabbi Ishmael said: Immediately Rabbi Nehuniah ben Ha-Kanah took hold of me and took me from my father’s house and brought me into the Chamber of Hewn Stone, and he adjured me with a great seal, with a great oath, in the name of Yad Azuf, Yad Azuy, Yad Hiraz, Yad Tekatz, with his great seal: by Zavandiel Yah, by Akatriel Yah, in heaven and on earth. And as soon as I heard this great mystery, my eyes were enlightened, and everything that I heard—Scripture, Mishnah, or any other matter—I would never forget again. The world was renewed in purity, and it was as if I had come from a new world.
1.3: And now, every student who knows that his learning does not succeed his learning is sustained in his hand, let him stand and bless, and let him arise and adjure in the name of Marganavel, Nite'el, Nite'el, Tariel, Haziyahyah, Sin, Sun, Suvirahu—all of them are Metatron the King; this is Metatron, Nu is Metatron, Tariel is Metatron, Haziyahyah is Metatron, Sin is Metatron, Sun is Metatron, Suvirahu is Metatron; and out of the love that He loves them, in the place where they say to him: Nite'el is a servant, and Muriel Yah, Akatriel YHVH God of Israel, YHVH YHVH, a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love and truth. Blessed is the Knower of Secrets and the Lord of Mysteries.

2.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: How does a man make use of this Crown? His mouth shall utter the Names and his fingers shall count one hundred and eighteen times; he shall not decrease nor shall he increase, and if he adds to them, the weight of his blood is upon his head. And the one who adjures shall stand, live, and sustain himself in the name of Marganavel, as in the first chapter, until he reaches "slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love." Blessed art Thou, O Lord, who revives the dead.
2.2: 2. Rabbi Ishmael said: Every disciple of the wise who recites this great secret—his stature is handsome for him, his speech is accepted, his awe is cast upon the creatures, his dreams are settled upon him, and he is saved from all kinds of calamities, sorceries, and the judgment of Gehenna.
2.3: And Rabbi Ishmael said: Every disciple of the wise who recites this great secret should recite them in bed and say: "Blessed art Thou, O Lord, to the knowledge of Your statutes; You are good and do good, teach me Your statutes."
2.4: Rabbi Ishmael said: When I was thirteen years old, my heart stirred with this matter, and I returned to my teacher, Rabbi Nehuniah ben Ha-Kanah. [I said,] "My Master, you gave me the Prince of the Torah—what is his name?" And he gave me: Yofiel is his name. Immediately I stood and afflicted myself for forty days, and I uttered the name of the Great One until I brought him down. And he descended in a flame of fire, and his face was like the appearance of lightning. When I saw him, I was terrified and I trembled and retreated backward. And he said to me: "Son of man, what is your nature that you have disturbed the Great Entourage?" And I said to him: "It is revealed and known before Him who spoke and the world came into being … "
2.5: And it was for the sake of the world that I did not bring you down for your own honor, but to do the will of your Maker. And also for me, son of man—a putrid drop, maggot and worm—whoever desires that [this] should come upon him, let him sit in a fast for forty days, and let him immerse twenty-four immersions each day, and let him not taste any defiled thing. And let him not gaze upon a woman, and let him sit in a dark house in peace.
2.6: In the name of Namnu’a Keter ‘A Tartia Kassan Kisse Yated Shalom Damli Aut Itkaut Ha’ul Ha’ul Tzavich Tzaviv Haviv Anhon Saskyah Dekach Hamyah Hazdakah She-na Sanvich Haz Kerad Nifrazah; YHVH shall direct us, my brothers, and we shall be beautified. Blessed be the name of His glory.
2.7: In the name of Ehyeh Kamush Yikrerah Kassan Kisse Yated Olam Ak Ant Tzaviv Aviv Hayah YHVH of Hosts, Mighty Lord, Ah YHVH of Hosts Holy, Holy, Holy; Blessed be the name of the glory of His kingdom forever and ever. Finished.
